title: Effective descent of smooth groups over fields and traits
statement: Let $B\to C$ be a faithfully flat ring homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] such that either both rings are fields [def-weil-field] or both rings are discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $S'=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $G'$ be a smooth separated finite-type $S'$-group scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; a group scheme has multiplication, inverse and identity over its base satisfying the group-object diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], and separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose $G'$ has a descent datum [def-pd-descent-datum] relative to $S'\to S$ whose isomorphism over $S'\times_SS'$ is a group isomorphism [def-pc-base-change]. Then there are a smooth separated finite-type $S$-group scheme $G$ and an $S'$-group isomorphism $G\times_SS'\simeq G'$ realizing the given datum. Neither affineness nor projectivity of $G'$ is assumed.

source.place: 6.5 Theorem 1, printed p.157 (PDF p.163), group-scheme case (take the torsor to be the group itself); primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Write $p:S'\to S$. Faithful flatness of $B\to C$ gives flatness of $p$ and surjectivity on spectra by the cited ring-to-scheme and spectrum lemmas. Since $p^{-1}(S)=S'$ is affine, the one-member affine cover $\{S\}$ of $S$ shows that $p$ is affine by the affine-local-target criterion, so $p$ is quasi-compact by affine-morphism permanence. Thus $\{p\}$ is an fpqc covering. This checks the covering hypothesis for every descent theorem below.

source.place: BLR 6.1 covering hypotheses and the cited ring-to-scheme, surjective-spectrum and affine-morphism permanence statements.

proof.text: If $B,C$ are fields, the finite-type group $G'$ carries an ample module by the field-group ampleness lemma. Apply field ample-scheme datum effectivity; this yields the underlying descended scheme with the prescribed datum. Proceed to the last step. Otherwise let $K=\operatorname{Frac}B$, $L=\operatorname{Frac}C$. The generic fibre $G'_L$ is a separated finite-type $L$-group: pull back its three structural maps and their identities, and use separatedness, local finite-type and quasi-compact base-change permanence. Field-group ampleness and field ample-scheme datum effectivity give a $K$-scheme $X_0$ with $X_0\times_KL\simeq G'_L$ realizing the generic restriction of the datum.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Theorem 1 proof, first paragraph, printed p.160; Stacks Tag 0BF7 for the existing field-group ampleness input.

proof.text: In the DVR case, apply the generic-effectivity affine-open lemma to $X'=G'$ and $X_0$. Obtain an invariant affine open $U'\subseteq G'$, dense in every geometric fibre, and an affine effective model $U$ over $B$ with $U_K\hookrightarrow X_0$. Apply the horizontal-boundary lemma to precisely these models and this open. It supplies $D_0$ and its Cartier closure $D'$, supported on $G'\setminus U'$, together with a cocycle-compatible datum on $M'=\mathcal O_{G'}(D')$. In particular this is a datum on a specified line bundle, not just invariance of its isomorphism class.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Theorem 1 proof, final reduction on printed pp.161-162 and boundary construction in case (a), p.160.

proof.text: The DVR $C$ is Noetherian because each ideal is principal; it has dimension one by the DVR dimension lemma and is integrally closed by valuation-ring normality. Let $H=(G')^0$ be the relative neutral open subgroup. Its fibres are geometrically connected and its geometric orbits on $G'$ are the connected components, by the neutral-open lemma. Since $U'$ is fibrewise dense, it meets every such orbit. Consequently $H\times_{S'}U'\to G'$ is surjective on underlying points: after passing to an algebraic closure of a residue field, a point and any point of $U'$ in its component differ by an element of $H$. Apply the Dedekind action-boundary ampleness lemma to the left action of $H$ on $G'$ and to $D'$. Its conclusion says exactly that $M'$ is ample. Polarized affine fpqc effectivity now produces an underlying $S$-scheme $G$ and an isomorphism $G\times_SS'\simeq G'$ realizing the given datum.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Theorem 1 proof, case (a), printed p.160, with 6.4 Proposition 2 and the neutral-open paragraph following it; 6.1 Theorem 7.

proof.text: In either case, transport multiplication, inverse and identity through the effective isomorphism. Their compatibility with the prescribed datum lets the fpqc morphism-descent bijection descend them to $G\times_SG\to G$, $G\to G$ and $S\to G$. Apply its injectivity to the two sides of each associativity, unit and inverse identity; after pullback they are the given identities of $G'$, so they agree over $S$. Thus $G$ is a group scheme and the effective isomorphism is a group isomorphism. Finally smoothness and separatedness descend by the two cited fpqc locality statements. Local finite type and quasi-compactness descend separately by their cited statements, and together mean finite type. All these tests concern the already constructed scheme $G$; none asserts general effectivity of scheme descent.

source.place: BLR 6.5 opening discussion and Theorem 1, printed pp.156-157; Stacks Tags 02W0, 02VL, 02KU, 02KX, 02KQ.
